assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength idea with Ye's demonstration of extreme coherence and systematic control. It brought timekeeping to the 10^-18 level, which is a quantitative leap rather than an incremental improvement. It also turns atomic structure and many-body physics into a precision tool for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift at the millimetre scale and, prospectively, a redefinition of the second. This is exactly the kind of precise, interpretable atomic physics I trust.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the early strontium clock. Ye's JILA group drove the performance to the current record levels. Others (for example Lemonde, Gill, Hollberg, Wineland-style ion clocks) contributed to the broader field, but the supplied credit is compact and the two-person split is natural and defensible.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories worldwide (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, SYRTE, PTB, NIST, NPL) have reproduced and exceeded the early results. Clock comparisons over fibre links and the geodesy demonstrations are well established. Recognition is timely, since Hall and Haensch (frequency combs, 2005) and Wineland (2012) already prepared the ground.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to separate the lattice-clock concept from the ion-clock and frequency-comb lineage, which have already been recognised.
Other contributors (for example Pierre Lemonde, Patrick Gill) are not among the supplied credited names.
Practical impact (redefinition of the second) is still pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices make clean, tunable quantum many-body systems: the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, quantum gas microscopes and later quantum simulation of Hubbard-type models. The proposal-to-experiment arc is a model of how a fundamental question (how do strongly correlated phases emerge?) can be addressed in a controllable system. Conceptually rich and widely emulated.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) supplied the key theoretical proposals, Greiner's 2002 Mott-insulator experiment with Haensch and Bloch was the decisive demonstration, and Bloch built the field and quantum-gas microscopy ecosystem. Cirac and Esslinger are also strongly credited and the three-name limit forces a hard choice. The same names recur in B035 and B036, so any prize here interacts with those candidates.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. Reproduced by dozens of groups, and the Mott transition, Fermi-Hubbard antiferromagnetic correlations and microscopy are firmly established. Timely, and arguably overdue after the 2001 BEC prize.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Cirac and Esslinger is genuinely contested and not resolved by the supplied list.
Overlap with the trapped-ion and Rydberg candidates may split support for Zoller and Cirac.
Whether it is a single discovery or a broad programme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms is the cleanest demonstration that massive particles show wave interference, and it has become the basis of the most sensitive inertial and gravitational measurements (gravimeters, gradiometers, tests of the equivalence principle and measurements of G and alpha). It speaks directly to the boundary between quantum and classical behaviour that I care about, and to precision.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard demonstrated early atom interferometry with gratings and later contributed to precision measurements. Kasevich and Chu (not listed) developed light-pulse interferometers for inertial sensing, and Bordé provided the theory of the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer. Schmiedmayer is credited for atom chips and coherent manipulation. Selecting three from four is difficult, and Chu's absence from the list limits a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature in laboratory precision and now being deployed in field sensors. Large-scale fundamental tests (long-baseline interferometers) are still in progress, and some headline claims of sensitivity to dark matter or gravitational waves remain prospective.
uncertainties: Steven Chu, an obvious contributor, is not in the credited names, and he has already received a prize for related cooling work.
Priority questions among Pritchard, Kasevich, Bordé and Schmiedmayer.
Applications may outpace fundamental discovery content.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of a magic angle with flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018 opened a new field of moire quantum materials that is genuinely unexpected: strong correlation from a purely geometric tuning knob in a carbon material. The conceptual simplicity of the picture (two rotated lattices) is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction. Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experiments with Cao and Fatemi (students). A fair three-way split is feasible, though the experimental team beyond the senior author is large.
assessment.maturity: Several groups reproduced the correlated states in a few years, and the field has expanded to many moire systems. Superconducting mechanism and the many competing phases are not settled, which makes the prize somewhat early, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Nature of the superconductivity and the correlated insulators remains debated.
Sample dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate comparisons.
The 2018 timing may be premature compared with candidates of more than two decades' standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising strongly interacting Fermi gases tuned through a Feshbach resonance, and observing the crossover from molecular BEC to BCS-type fermionic pairs, connects ultracold atoms to superconductivity and neutron-star matter. The unitary Fermi gas is a universal strongly interacting system with a clear measurable equation of state and sound propagation.
assessment.attribution: Experimental groups of Grimm (molecular BEC, pair condensates), Salomon (collective modes, equation of state), Thomas (unitary gas, early strongly interacting gas) and Jin and Ketterle (Jin deceased in 2016, and not eligible) all contributed in 2002-2004. Jin's death makes the prize configuration harder, and the supplied three names exclude Ketterle, who already has a prize.
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently reproduced. The phase diagram, superfluid transition temperature and spectral properties have been confirmed by multiple methods. Timely or slightly late.
uncertainties: Posthumous contribution of Deborah Jin cannot be recognised.
Priority among simultaneous 2003-2004 experiments is intricate.
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with the optical-lattice candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and their association with a blazar flare (TXS 0506+056) opened a new window on the cosmos, and IceCube's kilometre-cubed detector in Antarctic ice is a remarkable instrument. The finding is new and unexpected in its details. As an atomic physicist I am more cautious on astrophysics, but the clarity of the discovery is high.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA. Large-collaboration credit, with other leaders (for example Olga Botner, Albrecht Karle, Christian Spiering) not on the supplied list, makes a single-name prize hard to justify on this packet alone.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed at high significance, and the Galactic plane neutrino map and NGC 1068 results are additional, but the source identification is still partly open. Reasonably mature but not final.
uncertainties: Only one credited name is supplied, and the committee may want a broader attribution.
Source population remains largely unidentified.
I defer to colleagues in astroparticle physics on the strength of the evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's geometric phase show that phases in quantum mechanics carry physical, topological information beyond local fields. They underpin much of modern physics, from molecular dynamics to topological band theory. It is the kind of unexpected conceptual insight about quantum mechanics I find most compelling.
assessment.attribution: The Aharonov-Bohm effect (1959) was published by Aharonov and David Bohm, and Bohm died in 1992, so only Aharonov can be honoured. Berry's 1984 geometric phase is clearly his, with related work by Pancharatnam, Simon and others. Two laureates are plausible, though the two discoveries are separate and the combination is somewhat artificial.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades (Chambers 1960, Tonomura 1986, many Berry-phase experiments). The question is timeliness, as the discoveries are old, and the committee has historically hesitated to reward concepts of such age.
uncertainties: Bohm is deceased and cannot share the prize.
Two distinct discoveries combined into one candidate.
Very old discoveries may sit awkwardly with recent-impact criteria.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kilonovae establish neutron-star mergers as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis, and AT2017gfo, following GW170817, was a decisive multi-messenger observation. It answers a long-standing question about the origin of heavy elements, although the multi-messenger discovery was partly recognised through the 2017 gravitational-wave prize.
assessment.attribution: Metzger led the theory of radioactively powered transients, Kasen the detailed radiative transfer and opacity modelling, and Foley the discovery team of the optical counterpart (with Coulter, Kilpatrick and others). The experimental discovery was a large collaborative effort, so the attribution is difficult and the 1998 Li and Paczynski proposal is not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Based largely on one exceptionally well-observed event, so independent confirmation is limited. Subsequent events (GRB 230307A with JWST) add support, but the r-process yield interpretation is still debated.
uncertainties: The key evidence is essentially a single event, which gives me pause.
Interpretation of opacities and lanthanide production is uncertain.
I defer to astrophysics colleagues, and the discovery is partly covered by the 2017 prize.
